title: Minimum Energy to Maintain Brightness
summary: Given an integer n representing n light bulbs arranged in a line and indexed from 0 to n-1 , an integer brightness, and a 2D integer array intervals where each interval [start_i, end_i] represents an inclusive time period during which the total illumination must meet or exceed the brightness requirement, determine the minimum total energy required.
statement: Given an integer n representing n light bulbs arranged in a line and indexed from 0 to n-1 , an integer brightness, and a 2D integer array intervals where each interval [start_i, end_i] represents an inclusive time period during which the total illumination must meet or exceed the brightness requirement, determine the minimum total energy required. Each bulb consumes 1 unit of energy per time unit it is on. A bulb illuminates its own position and its adjacent positions within the interval. The total illumination is the count of illuminated positions, with each position counted at most once.
constraints: There are n bulbs in a line; an active interior bulb can illuminate its own and adjacent positions.
During every inclusive time interval, total illuminated positions must be at least brightness; overlapping requirements are not additive.
hints: One active bulb contributes illumination to at most three positions, so ceil(brightness/3) bulbs are necessary and sufficient.
Merge overlapping required time intervals so shared times are paid once.
Multiply required bulbs by the total inclusive length of the interval union.
The spatial optimum is identical at each required time, while interval union accounts for exactly those times.
editorial: The spatial optimum is identical at each required time, while interval union accounts for exactly those times.

tests.explanation: Two bulbs cover at least five positions for seven time units, costing fourteen.
The union is times one through four and one bulb suffices, costing four.
